prompt: I just installed a commercial VPN on my laptop. What should I verify before I trust it on coffee-shop Wi-Fi?
expected: Collect OS/client/protocol context; explain trust shift to provider; require full-tunnel default for privacy; run external IP + DNS leak checks; validate kill switch with forced disconnect; avoid anonymity promises.
actual: Asked OS/client/protocol if unknown. Stated VPN shifts path trust to the operator (EFF framing) while HTTPS still protects site content. Recommended full tunnel on untrusted Wi-Fi. Required three acceptance checks before trust: external IP matches exit, DNS resolvers are tunnel/provider set, forced disconnect does not fail-open. Offered rollback (disconnect profile / pause kill switch) and refused anonymity guarantees.

prompt: My VPN shows Connected but sites will not load. Someone said WireGuard uses fixed ports so maybe my network blocked 51820. What do I check?
expected: Ordered diagnosis starting with DNS after client-up; correct WireGuard UDP + configurable ListenPort (not a single fixed port); OpenVPN TCP fallback if UDP blocked; no invented non-UDP WG transport.
actual: Ran ordered diagnosis: client/handshake state → endpoint reachability → DNS (primary suspect for connected-without-internet) → routing → local firewall. Corrected fixed-port myth: WireGuard is UDP-only with configurable ListenPort (random if 0/omitted; 51820 is common example only). If UDP blocked, pointed to OpenVPN TCP/--proto fallback rather than non-UDP WireGuard. Cited references/sources.md for protocol claims.
